walkthrough:
In right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$ (with $\angle BAC = \frac{\pi}{2}$ and $\angle ABC = \frac{\pi}{5}$), calculate angle $\angle ACD$:
$$\angle ACD = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{5} = \frac{3\pi}{10}\text{ radians}$$

Because line $BC$ is tangent to the circular arc $DE$ at point $D$, the radius $AD$ is perpendicular to $BC$ ($AD \perp BC$). In the right-angled triangle $\triangle ADC$:
$$AD = AC\sin(\angle ACD) = 8\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{10}\right) = 8\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{5}\right)$$
$$AD \approx 8(0.809017) \approx 6.4721 \approx 6.47\text{ cm} \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$

skill_tags: Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regions

hints: Sum both areas to find the total shaded area.
walkthrough:
Calculate the angle of sector $ADE$ at centre $A$:
$$\angle EAD = \angle BAC - \angle DAC = \frac{\pi}{2} - \left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{3\pi}{10}\right) = \frac{3\pi}{10}\text{ radians}$$

Calculate the area of sector $ADE$ (with radius $AD = 6.4721\text{ cm}$):
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } ADE) = \frac{1}{2}(AD)^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(6.4721)^2\left(\frac{3\pi}{10}\right) \approx \frac{1}{2}(41.888)(0.94248) \approx 19.740\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of right-angled triangle $\triangle ADC$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle ADC) = \frac{1}{2}(AC)(AD)\sin(\angle DAC) = \frac{1}{2}(8)(6.4721)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{5}\right) \approx 25.8884(0.58779) \approx 15.217\text{ cm}^2$$

Sum the areas of the sector and triangle to obtain the total shaded area:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = 19.740 + 15.217 = 34.957 \approx 35.0\text{ cm}^2 \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$

ai_rubric.Circular Measure and Area: Calculates sector area $\approx 19.74$ (M1). Calculates triangle area $\approx 15.22$ (M1). Obtains shaded area $35.0\text{ cm}^2$ (A1).
